findings.title: lineage /upstream: 404 vs 200 [] leaks UUID existence
findings.first_evidence: pcs-backend/app/api/v1/lineage.py:210 -- raise HTTPException(404, "no lineage for record")
findings.why_it_matters: The batch's stated security property is that 'no access' and 'does not exist' must be byte-identical so UUIDs cannot be enumerated. _guard_record_access returns silently when the record does not exist, so GET /lineage/streams/{uuid}/upstream answers 200 with an empty list for a UUID that does not exist, while the same endpoint answers 404 'no lineage for record' for a UUID that exists in another project: the response difference is an existence oracle (the /graph and /downstream suffixes already answer 404 for both). Reproduced against the reviewed head - a nonexistent UUID returns 200 [] on /upstream and 404 on /graph and /downstream, while a cross-project stream returns 404 on all three.
findings.suggested_fix: Make all three lineage endpoints share one 'no lineage' shape. In app/api/v1/lineage.py::_guard_record_access, replace the silent `return` for a missing record with the same exception used for the no-access case (`raise HTTPException(404, "no lineage for record")`), so 'missing' and 'not mine' are indistinguishable on every suffix while an authorized record that simply has no lineage still returns 200 []. Correct the stale comment at lineage.py:201 that claims the endpoint 'naturally 404s'. Extend tests/api/v1/test_lineage_guard.py::test_lineage_cross_project_looks_identical_to_missing to be parametrized over ['/graph', '/upstream', '/downstream'] and assert identical status_code, code and message between the missing-id and the cross-project-id response. Assumption: the frontend only consumes /graph (pcs-frontend/src/pages/sim/tabs/StreamLineageTab.tsx), so the empty-list case of /upstream is not relied upon by the UI.

findings.title: review-log endpoint never returns check pass/reject rows
findings.why_it_matters: The new GET /streams/{id}/review-log is documented to return the three review transitions (SUBMIT_FOR_CHECK / PASS_CHECK / REJECT_CHECK), but its query filters `AuditLog.action == "RECORD_TRANSITION"` while the state machine writes APPROVAL_STEP_PASSED / APPROVAL_STEP_REJECTED for PASS_CHECK / REJECT_CHECK (TRANSITION_AUDIT_ACTION, app/services/state_machine.py:121-123). The check verdicts are therefore dropped and the endpoint can only ever return the submit row - the failure is silent (200 + partial list), so a designer never sees 校对通过 or 校对驳回, which is the whole content TODO-112 exists to deliver. The new test hides it: tests/api/v1/test_stream_review_log.py:95 fabricates action="RECORD_TRANSITION" rows for all three transitions, a shape production never writes, so the suite is green on impossible data.
findings.suggested_fix: Stop filtering on a single audit action: the rows are already scoped by `resource_type='streams'` + `resource_id`, and the `detail_json->>'transition' IN ('SUBMIT_FOR_CHECK','PASS_CHECK','REJECT_CHECK')` predicate is the authoritative selector (the state machine writes detail_json['transition'] for every transition, including PASS/REJECT). Either drop the `AuditLog.action == "RECORD_TRANSITION"` predicate, or widen it to `AuditLog.action.in_(("RECORD_TRANSITION", "APPROVAL_STEP_PASSED", "APPROVAL_STEP_REJECTED"))` derived from TRANSITION_AUDIT_ACTION so the two lists cannot drift. Then fix tests/api/v1/test_stream_review_log.py:95 so the fixture derives the action from the state machine's own mapping (TRANSITION_AUDIT_ACTION[StateTransition[transition]].value) and assert that a PASS_CHECK and a REJECT_CHECK row actually appear in the response - otherwise the suite cannot catch this regression again. The frontend MSW mock (pcs-frontend/src/mocks/handlers.ts) fabricates the same impossible PASS_CHECK row and must be aligned.

findings.title: batch guard DB failure skips the rollback and poisons the rest of the batch
findings.first_evidence: pcs-backend/app/services/stream_batch_service.py:284 — `    if not await has_project_access(` (executed after `stream = await select_stream_for_update(db, stream_id)` at line 260, i.e. with the row lock already held; the release call `_release_precheck_transaction(db)` at line 290 is only reached when the call RETURNS False, not when it RAISES)
findings.why_it_matters: The new project guard (has_project_access) is a database call inside _submit_one_inner. When it raises, _submit_one's blanket `except Exception` turns it into an INTERNAL_ERROR failed item - but nothing rolls the session back, so the transaction stays open with the SELECT ... FOR UPDATE row lock still held. The transition path has exactly this rollback (stream_batch_service.py:363) and the existing test test_db_level_failure_does_not_poison_the_rest_of_the_batch only covers that path. After one guard failure the session is poisoned: on PostgreSQL the transaction is aborted, so every later item in the batch fails too and the row locks accumulate - which breaks the batch's own 'one item's failure must not affect the others' contract.
findings.suggested_fix: Either release the transaction before the guard call, or make the failure path safe. Preferred: resolve the owning project with a non-locking read (select(Stream.project_id).where(Stream.stream_id == stream_id)), check access on that, and only then take the locking read for the actual transition - a DB failure in the guard then happens outside the locked window. If the guard must stay inside the lock, wrap it in try/except and `await db.rollback()` before re-raising, and release the precheck transaction on the denied branch. Add a test that makes the guard's SELECT fail and asserts the following item still succeeds, and one that asserts db.in_transaction() is False after the guard's early return.

findings.title: review-log transition vocabulary is hand-written and the contract carries a bare string
findings.why_it_matters: OpenAPI declares ReviewLogItem.transition as a bare {"type": "string"} with the three-value vocabulary only in prose, and the service keeps its own hand-written copy of that vocabulary (REVIEW_TRANSITIONS = ('SUBMIT_FOR_CHECK', 'PASS_CHECK', 'REJECT_CHECK') in stream_review_log_service.py, a literal copy of StateTransition's values). The endpoint's own docstring claims this is the only copy of the vocabulary, but two copies exist. If a StateTransition value is renamed the endpoint silently returns [] (or a partial list) with no error - the Tab just shows '（无校核记录）', indistinguishable from 'never reviewed' - and no OpenAPI or type check can see the drift because the contract does not record the vocabulary. The frontend keeps a third copy in TRANSITION_LABEL.
findings.suggested_fix: Define the vocabulary once and derive every copy from it. In app/schemas/stream_review_log.py define ReviewTransition = Literal["SUBMIT_FOR_CHECK", "PASS_CHECK", "REJECT_CHECK"] (or a StrEnum) and annotate the field with it, so OpenAPI carries the enum and the frontend's components['schemas']['ReviewLogItem']['transition'] becomes a literal union; then let stream_review_log_service.REVIEW_TRANSITIONS derive from that Literal (the service already imports the schema, no circular import) or directly from StateTransition, and derive the audit-action list from TRANSITION_AUDIT_ACTION rather than re-typing it. Assert the derivation structurally (REVIEW_TRANSITIONS == tuple(t.value for t in (...))) so a rename fails a test instead of emptying a Tab.

findings.title: review-log MSW mock is not contract-derived and fabricates an impossible row
findings.why_it_matters: In dev/MSW mode the review-log handler returns the same two inline rows for every stream_id: a SUBMIT_FOR_CHECK row and a PASS_CHECK row that the real backend cannot produce (its action filter only ever returns RECORD_TRANSITION rows). The mock also hides the empty state and the 404 shape that the backend now defines, so the browser regression of this batch reported a 200 and two rows for data the real endpoint never returns - which is exactly how the backend's own filter bug survived the batch's QA.

findings.title: grant_project_access commits internally, breaking create_project's atomicity
findings.first_evidence: pcs-backend/app/api/v1/projects.py:115-116 -- 建行 + 绑矩阵 + 建默认矩阵模板 + **授权创建者**在**同一事务**里 ⇒ / 任一步失败**全回滚** ⇒ 不会留下「项目建好了但送不了审」或
findings.why_it_matters: create_project's docstring promises that creating the project, binding the default matrix and granting the creator all happen in one transaction and roll back together. But UserProjectService.grant_project_access commits internally, so the transaction is already committed before the endpoint's own `await db.commit()` at line 195 (which then commits nothing). Any failure after that commit - the db.refresh of the record, or response serialisation - returns an error to the client for a project that was actually created, and the endpoint's own error path reports it as 'not created'. The atomicity claim in the docstring is therefore not true for the whole endpoint.
findings.suggested_fix: Give grant_project_access a commit-free variant (e.g. grant_project_access(session, ..., commit: bool = True)) and call it with commit=False from create_project, so the endpoint keeps exactly one commit point at the end and the 'all-or-nothing' property is enforced by the endpoint. If the commit-free variant is not acceptable, at minimum replace the trailing `await db.commit()` + `await db.refresh(record)` with a comment acknowledging that the commit already happened inside the helper, and have the endpoint's post-commit error path report a distinct error code (e.g. PROJECT_CREATED_BUT_RESPONSE_FAILED) so the operator can distinguish 'not created' from 'created, response lost'. Assumption: no other caller of grant_project_access depends on it committing.

findings.title: not-found error text is hand-written in several places instead of derived
findings.why_it_matters: The 'no access == does not exist' invariant this batch is built on rests on the two guard branches producing byte-identical text. _load_stream_guarded writes the literal f"Stream {stream_id} 不存在" twice (the not-found branch and the no-access branch), and that literal is a further copy of the one in StreamService.get (app/services/stream_service.py:331 and :517); the state-point message and lineage.py's "no lineage for record" (three occurrences) and the batch's f"物流 {stream_id} 不存在" (two occurrences in stream_batch_service.py) are duplicated the same way. The repo's own rule for this batch says same-shape must come from one helper, not from two copies of the same words - and the same-shape tests only compare the two guard branches with each other, never against StreamService.get. If the service rewords its 404, or a future endpoint routes around the guard, the enumeration vector returns with the whole suite still green.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep one canonical error per layer and have the guard reuse it: give StreamService a single factory (e.g. StreamService.stream_not_found_error(stream_id) / state_point_not_found_error(state_point_id)) used by get/get_state_point AND by _load_stream_guarded / _load_state_point_guarded; in stream_batch_service.py extract one local _not_found_item(stream_id) used by both the real not-found branch and the new guard branch, so the two copies cannot diverge; and keep one "no lineage for record" constant in lineage.py. Then pin the structure rather than the text: assert both branches raise the same constructed error (e.g. compare the exception object or the code, not a re-typed string), and add the service's own 404 envelope to the same-shape assertion so a service-side reword is caught.

findings.title: batch takes a row lock on a foreign stream before the access check
findings.why_it_matters: In the batch submit path the project guard runs AFTER select_stream_for_update, so a caller with access only to project A can take a SELECT ... FOR UPDATE lock on a stream that belongs to project B before the access check rejects the item. The lock is released immediately afterwards by _release_precheck_transaction, so this is a lock-ordering side channel rather than a durable deadlock - but a caller can briefly block another project's writer on that row.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve the owning project without locking, check access, then take the lock: before select_stream_for_update, do a plain select(Stream.project_id).where(Stream.stream_id == stream_id) (non-locking), call has_project_access() on that project_id and return the identical SIM_STREAM_NOT_FOUND failed item when access is denied; only then call select_stream_for_update() for the actual work. Assumption: a stream's project_id never changes after creation, so the unlocked read cannot be used to smuggle a project switch; re-check access after locking if that invariant ever changes. This is the same restructuring that removes the poisoned-session window in the guard's failure path.

findings.title: ensure_user_row and grant_project_access are lock-free get-or-creates with no savepoint
findings.why_it_matters: ensure_user_row does SELECT-by-user_id, then SELECT-by-username, then session.add(row) + await session.flush() with no savepoint, no IntegrityError recovery and no re-read of the winner - on a column (users.username) that is unique. This path is newly reachable from a user-facing write: per ADR-0046 section 3b a mock login never creates a users row, so the row is genuinely absent on the first call, and two concurrent POST /projects by the same user (double click, form resubmit) both see 'no row' and both INSERT. The loser hits the unique constraint with an uncaught IntegrityError - a 500 that also rolls back the whole project creation. The same shape exists in grant_project_access (user_project_service.py:83-107), which is pre-existing but newly reachable from create_project: a lock-free SELECT-then-INSERT against user_projects' unique(user_id, project_id).
findings.suggested_fix: Apply the repository's recorded get-or-create recipe to both functions: wrap the INSERT in `async with db.begin_nested():` with db.add() inside the savepoint, and on IntegrityError re-read the winning row and return it read-only (never overwrite the winner's columns), re-raising if the violated constraint is not the expected one. The repo's own knowledge base (docs/solutions/database-issues/get-or-create-default-row-race-savepoint-reread.md) records this shape and names the correctly-fixed sibling (_get_or_create_default_record_matrix) in the same file that neither new path copies. Do not use a bare db.rollback() for the recovery - the caller's project INSERT is in the same transaction.
